clearing_status.fact: On Feb 25, 2025, the SEC formally extended compliance dates by one year (Release 34-102487): cash from Dec 31 2025 to Dec 31 2026, repo from Jun 30 2026 to Jun 30 2027. Separately, on Apr 17 2026 the SEC published a SIFMA exemptive-relief request (inter-affiliate exemption expansion) with a public comment deadline of May 29 2026 (TBAC Charge Q2 2026, treasury.gov, dated May 2026). As of Aug 2026, the SEC reaffirmed the current deadlines with no second extension (SEC Commissioner Uyeda statement, sec.gov, ~Aug 7 2026).
clearing_status.rationale: One official one-year extension has already been granted (rubric = 1), and a SIFMA exemptive-relief request was pending as of May 2026 (also independently triggering rubric = 1). No second formal extension has been announced as of Aug 17 2026, so rubric level 2 is not met.

dissent.view: DTCC Aug 2026 readiness survey finds industry 'well positioned' for Dec 31 2026 cash deadline with >$1.2T already clearing, suggesting operational trajectory closer to on-track; however the prior formal extension and pending exemptive relief request still satisfy rubric = 1.

plan_financing.fact: 10-year JGB yield touched 2.93% on Aug 17 2026 — its highest since September 1996 — driven by fiscal concerns over PM Takaichi's stimulus spending plans; yield is up ~130 bps over 12 months and ~19 bps over the past month. Funding path was specified (deficit-covering bonds, no new net issuance per May 2026 supplementary budget), but markets have continuously repriced higher. No failed auction (BTC <2) or BOJ emergency operation found; Aug 4 2026 10Y auction cleared per MOF. Sources: Euronews 2026-08-17 (https://www.euronews.com/business/2026/08/17/japans-10-year-bond-yield-hits-a-30-year-high-as-growth-data-disappoints); TradingEconomics 2026-08-14; MOF auction result page 2026-08-04 (https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/eresul/eresul20260804a.htm); CNBC 2026-06-01 (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/01/japan-pm-takaichis-budget-remarks-send-red-flag-to-bond-markets.html).
plan_financing.rationale: The 10Y JGB yield is up far more than 25 bps on fiscal news (rubric score 1 threshold) and the funding path, while nominally specified, has not been credibly accepted by markets — qualifying as UNCLEAR. However, without a confirmed failed/tailing auction (BTC <2) or BOJ emergency operation, the evidence does not reach the DISORDERLY threshold (score 2), per the instruction not to assign the most severe level without clear evidence.

dissent.view: ModelDiplomat (July 2026) argues a near-term disorderly unwind is 'unlikely' given Japan's domestic investor base, long debt-maturity profile, and FY2026 primary-balance surplus, suggesting markets are stress-testing but not breaking.

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings LinkedIn post (August 2026) titled 'U.S. Private Credit Default Rate drops to 5.2% in July' signals the TTM Fitch PCDR fell to 5.2% for July 2026, down from the record 6.0% TTM confirmed in Fitch's Q2 2026 quarterly report published July 30 2026 (Bloomberg, Investment Executive, LSTA). The 6.0% Q2 figure itself was up from 5.7% in Q1 2026; Fitch recorded 32 default events from 20 new unique defaulters in Q2, with maturity extensions comprising more than half.
direct_lending_default.rationale: The rubric requires the Fitch inclusive measure (counting distressed exchanges and LMEs); the most recent Fitch signal is the July 2026 monthly PCDR at 5.2% TTM per Fitch's own LinkedIn post, representing a pullback from the Q2 record of 6.0% as older high-default months roll off the TTM window. Confidence is medium because only the LinkedIn title (not full report text) is accessible; the Q2 6.0% print (fully corroborated by Bloomberg and Investment Executive on July 30 2026) is retained as the last fully verified anchor.

dissent.view: Fitch Q2 2026 quarterly report (fully corroborated): TTM private credit default rate 6.0% through Q2-end, a record high, up from 5.7% in Q1 2026; 32 default events from 20 new unique defaulters; more than half involved maturity extensions

With Intelligence estimate: 'true' default rate approached 5% through first nine months of 2025 when selective defaults and LMEs included; headline rate remained below 2% for several years on narrow count-based measure
Moody's: distressed restructurings accounted for roughly 65% of all 2025 private credit defaults; excluding them produces headline rates of 1.6%-4.7%
Proskauer Private Credit Default Index (count-based, narrower methodology): typically 2-3 points lower than Fitch inclusive measure

redemption_gates.fact: In Q1-Q2 2026, >=6 of the largest private credit/BDC funds simultaneously hit or enforced quarterly repurchase caps: Blue Owl OBDC II (permanently gated, $1.6B), Blue Owl OCIC ($34B, 22%/18.8% requests capped at 5%), BlackRock HPS ($26B, 9.3% capped), Apollo Debt Solutions ($723M Q1 redemptions doubling cap), Ares flagship (11.6% capped), Morgan Stanley North Haven (10.9% capped), Oaktree Strategic Credit (6.8%/expanded to 7%), Cliffwater CCLFX ($42B, 14%/7%). Q2 2026: Apollo, Ares, BlackRock, Blackstone, Cliffwater all gated a second consecutive quarter. Combined gated AUM far exceeds $100B. Sources: CRS/Congress.gov (March 27 2026), ABF Journal (May 28 2026), AltsWire (May 17 2026), ZeroHedge/Bloomberg (July 2 2026), Perspective on Risk Substack (April 11 2026).
redemption_gates.rationale: More than 6 named funds spanning Apollo, Ares, BlackRock HPS, Blue Owl (multiple vehicles), Cliffwater, Morgan Stanley, and Oaktree enforced quarterly repurchase caps in the same Q1 2026 window, with gating persisting into Q2 2026; combined AUM of affected funds is estimated well above $100B, satisfying the rubric threshold for WIDESPREAD (>=3 largest funds or >$100B AUM gated in the same quarter).

dissent.view: Some analysts (CAIA, PGIM, Adams Street) argue gates are functioning as contractually designed structural safeguards, not evidence of credit distress or systemic liquidity failure; Blackstone BCRED avoided a hard gate by injecting $400M of own capital.

new_imf_programs.fact: Two new IMF lending arrangements were approved in the trailing 6 months: (1) Ukraine 48-month EFF ~US$8.1bn approved 26 Feb 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/02/26/pr-26066-ukraine); (2) Rwanda 36-month ECF ~US$250mn approved 8 Jun 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/06/08/pr26191). No sovereign missed coupon or new outright default by an EM sovereign was identified in the Feb–Aug 2026 window.
new_imf_programs.rationale: Two new IMF arrangements in the trailing 6 months maps exactly to the RISING band (1-2 new IMF arrangements); no missed coupon was found, and the count falls short of the >=3 threshold required for CLUSTER.

dissent.view: Ghana's July 27 2026 Board action included approval of a new 36-month Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI); if counted as a new 'arrangement' this would push the total to 3 and could support a CLUSTER reading, but a PCI is a non-financing, non-distress instrument and mainstream sovereign-credit practice excludes it from default-risk programme counts.

china_ppi.fact: NBS press release t20260810_1965017 (released 2026-08-10): 'In July 2026, China's producer price index for industrial products (PPI) increased by 3.5% year on year and decreased by 0.7% month on month.' Source: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260810_1965017.html
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric requires the signed NBS figure exactly as published; +3.5% YoY for July 2026 is confirmed by the primary NBS release dated 2026-08-10 and corroborated by Xinhua/China Daily. The engine scores on the SIZE of the move: +3.5% is a meaningful positive reading signalling cost-push input-price pressure being exported globally, though it moderated from June's +4.1%.

trade_actions.fact: In the trailing 3 months (mid-May to mid-Aug 2026), at least 8 distinct new measures were recorded: (1) USTR 12.5% Section 301 tariff on broad Chinese goods, effective 24 Jul 2026 (China Briefing, updated 24 Jul 2026; USTR); (2) US 15% tariffs on Chinese polysilicon + additional 12.5% Section 301 duties, announced 5 Aug 2026 (Polymarket summary); (3) China export controls on drone exports to US + ban on 6 US entities, 5 Aug 2026 (Fortune/Euronews); (4) China provisional anti-dumping deposits up to 54.3% on US/Mexican pecans, effective 11 Aug 2026 (MOFCOM/Global Times); (5) China export bans on 14 European companies, ~3 Aug 2026 (Mondaq/Steptoe); (6) EU definitive AD duty amendment on Chinese tinplate steel, 16 Apr 2026 (EU Reg. 2026/843); (7) UK definitive AD on Chinese tin mill products, 12 Mar 2026 (UK TRA); (8) US Commerce final LTFV determination on Chinese hardwood plywood, 21 Jul 2026 (Federal Register).
trade_actions.rationale: Eight distinct new measures across major economies (US, China, EU, UK) in the trailing 3 months, including a broad 12.5% Section 301 tariff across Chinese goods and explicit tit-for-tat export controls, exceeds the rubric threshold of >=4 new measures and includes a broad tariff round >=10% across a sector, mapping unambiguously to level 2 (ESCALATING). The underlying Nov 2025 truce framework remains nominally in place but is being actively eroded by new unilateral actions on both sides.

license_flow.fact: The April 2025 MOFCOM licensing regime (Announcement No. 28/related notices) requiring non-automatic, case-by-case export licences for dysprosium, terbium, and Dy/Tb-containing NdFeB and SmCo magnets was never suspended and remains fully in force as of August 2026. MOFCOM issued a first batch of general licences in December 2025 to three named large exporters (JL MAG / Jinli, San Huan, Zhongke Sanhuan, Yunsheng) but these cover only pre-vetted named customers and are not broadly available. Statutory review target is 45 working days (~9 weeks), but in practice heavy-REE approvals routinely run 60-120+ days; a June 2025 US-China diplomatic deal produced a MOFCOM statement to 'review and approve eligible applications in accordance with law' yet Trump's August 2026 threats of 200% tariffs signal Washington remains unsatisfied with throughput. The 2026 Import-Export Licensing Catalogue added samarium, gadolinium, and lutetium compounds as new controlled categories. Source: blog.gettransport.com (July 7 2026), china-briefing.com, merics.org, arnold magnetics (Feb 2026), certivo.com (March 2026).
license_flow.rationale: Licensing is case-by-case / whitelist (general licences restricted to a handful of named producers) with real-world processing times of 60-120+ days far exceeding the 30-day threshold, and new categories (samarium, gadolinium, lutetium compounds) were added to the control list in the trailing 3 months via the 2026 catalogue update — all three SLOWING triggers are met. No categorical denial to a country or announced licensing suspension exists that would support a FROZEN (2) rating, and market data show exports continuing at positive YoY growth, capping the escalation read at 1.

dissent.view: Duramag (Dec 2025) and Arnold Magnetics (Feb 2026) characterise approvals as 'rare, documentation-intensive and unpredictable' with applications on hold indefinitely, which could support a borderline FROZEN read for heavy-REE end-uses; however no MOFCOM-announced categorical denial or >30-day suspension of issuance is documented.
Tech-Insider (late July 2026) reports China widened controls to 10 US firms in June and 14 EU firms in July 2026, suggesting entity-level denials that edge toward FROZEN for specific counterparties.

truce_status.fact: The Nov-2025 Busan rare earth truce (nominal expiry 2026-11-10) is formally still in force but has been partially breached: on June 22, 2026, Beijing added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export-control entity blacklist (FDD analysis, fdd.org, 2026-06-24). Chinese customs data as of May 2026 showed heavy rare earth exports (yttrium, dysprosium, terbium) still ~50% below pre-controls levels (Mining Weekly/Reuters, 2026-05-13). No confirmed renewal or extension has been announced as of 2026-08-17, leaving ~85 days to the nominal expiry.
truce_status.rationale: Two rubric triggers for Score 1 are met simultaneously: (a) the truce is <90 days from its 2026-11-10 expiry with no renewal announced, and (b) a partial breach occurred on 2026-06-22 via new entity-list additions targeting the two largest US federally-funded rare earth firms, which China's own extraterritorial controls treat as a supply-chain cutoff mechanism.

dissent.view: A US official stated on 2026-05-11 that 'the deal is still in effect and an extension will be announced at the appropriate time' (Nikkei Asia/Reuters, 2026-05-11), suggesting the US government views the truce as formally intact despite the June entity-list action.

re_blacklist.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (issued 22 June 2026) added 10 named US entities to China's export control list, explicitly including MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc. The measure bars Chinese exporters from supplying dual-use items to the named firms and prohibits any party from transferring China-origin dual-use goods to them. Multiple corroborating sources (Benchmark Minerals, SMM/Metal.com, Trivium China, StockTitan citing Reuters) confirm the listing; market reaction was muted (MP Materials roughly flat, USA Rare Earth modestly higher on the day), consistent with an entity-specific rather than sector-wide ban. The restriction is explicitly firm-specific: 'The measure is entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US' (Benchmark Minerals, 25 June 2026).
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials and USA Rare Earth) appear by name on MOFCOM's export control list as of 22 June 2026, satisfying the rubric's definition of score 1 (entity-specific). The listing does not extend categorically to the US rare-earth sector as a class, and multiple analysts explicitly characterise it as firm-specific, precluding score 2.

hree_premium.fact: Rare Earth Exchanges (Aug 12, 2026) reports dysprosium oxide at $204-210/kg inside China (ACREI domestic reference) and assesses CIF Europe at ~$800/kg ex-China, implying a ~3.9x multiple; terbium shows a similar ~4x multiple ($990/kg domestic vs $4,000+/kg ex-China). Benchmark Minerals (Mar 24, 2026) put the 2025 dysprosium CIF North America multiple at 4.4x and forecast ~8.3x by 2027.
hree_premium.rationale: Applying the rubric to the load-bearing dysprosium price pair (domestic $207/kg vs ex-China CIF $800/kg as of Aug 12, 2026) yields a premium multiple of ~3.9x; this is corroborated by the terbium pair (~4.0x) and bracketed by the Benchmark 2025 actuals (4.4x) and Pentagon floor-implied low of ~2.8x, supporting a central reading near 3.9.

genius_impl.fact: The statutory one-year deadline of July 18, 2026 passed without any final rules from the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, Federal Reserve, FinCEN, or OFAC; all major rule packages remained at the proposed/comment stage, with some comment periods still open as late as August 21, 2026. Sources: Crowdfund Insider (July 2026): 'Federal banking and financial regulators have allowed the statutory one-year period for completing implementing regulations under the GENIUS Act to lapse without delivering finalized rules.' CoinPaprika (July 19, 2026): 'The Treasury Department and four primary regulators left every major rule package as a proposal.' OCC Bulletin 2026-3 (Feb 25, 2026) confirmed only an NPRM was issued.
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric level 2 requires the deadline to be missed without final rules; that condition is unambiguously met — the July 18, 2026 statutory deadline passed with zero finalized implementing regulations across all five responsible agencies, constituting a clear deadline miss with no court stay or compliance-failure event needed to trigger level 2.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Alphabet Q2 2026 (reported July 22, 2026): capex $44.9B, up ~100% YoY; Google Cloud revenue $24.8B, up 82% YoY, accelerating from ~63% in Q1 2026; full-year capex guidance raised to $195-$205B. Microsoft FY26 Q4 (June 30, 2026): Azure +43% YoY (accelerating); capex guided >$40B/quarter. Sources: SEC 8-K MSFT July 29 2026; Alphabet Q2 2026 earnings July 22 2026 (CNBC, Tickeron, BigGo Finance).
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~100% YoY for Alphabet, ~66%+ for Microsoft) materially exceeds AI-attributable revenue growth (~82% Cloud for Alphabet, ~43% Azure for Microsoft), keeping the gap wide; however, AI revenue is still accelerating QoQ (Alphabet Cloud 82% vs ~63% prior quarter; Azure 43% vs 40% prior quarter), and no hyperscaler cut its AI-revenue outlook, so rubric score 2 is not triggered.

dissent.view: Alphabet raised full-year capex guidance to $195-205B (from $180-190B) while FCF turned negative at -$5.9B and stock sold off 7% after-hours, which some analysts frame as capex outrunning monetization in a manner approaching rubric-2 severity

Nextwavesinsight pre-Q2 analysis citing Allianz Research estimated a ~46% capex-to-revenue divergence exceeding the 2001 telecom overbuild peak of 32%, suggesting systemic widening rather than idiosyncratic gap

gpu_refi_stress.fact: CoreWeave CDS priced at 855 bps (50% five-year default probability) on July 29 2026, and the company was forced to widen its $2.6B leveraged loan spread by 100-125 bps; separately, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, SMBC and MUFG spent 6+ months distributing $38B of Oracle-leased data-center construction debt, with some banks selling at a discount to non-bank lenders (Financial Times, reported May 6 2026; TechTimes CDS coverage July 30 2026; CNBC Q2 earnings Aug 11 2026).
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: Two rubric-1 triggers are simultaneously active: named banks offloading AI/data-center debt at a discount and CoreWeave, a named GPU-backed borrower, facing a documented refinancing wall with CDS-implied 50% default odds. However, CoreWeave's Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 11) beat consensus, interest expense landed at the low end of guidance, management affirmed no hard debt maturities until 2029, and no default or distressed exchange has been confirmed, keeping the reading at 1 rather than 2.

dissent.view: CoreWeave Q2 2026 earnings beat (revenue +112% YoY, $104B backlog, interest expense at low end of guidance at $640M) and new Anthropic/Meta contracts suggest near-term default risk is overstated by CDS market; equity analysts maintain average $145.76 Buy target

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: According to Trepp data cited by Colliers Knowledge Leader (April 8 2026): 'the office CMBS delinquency rate stood at 11.71% in March 2026, down from the 12.34% peak reached in January' — Trepp/Colliers, March 2026 reporting period.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The rubric calls for the latest Trepp CMBS office delinquency rate as a percent; 11.71% is the most recent explicitly published Trepp office-sector figure found (March 2026), with the January 2026 all-time high of 12.34% and a July 2026 overall spike of 51 bps suggesting the rate may be drifting higher again but no updated office sub-rate is available. Confidence is medium because the July 2026 Trepp report was not broken out by sector in available sources.

dissent.view: KBRA (not Trepp) reported its own-rated CMBS office delinquency at 13.9% in January 2026, 12.8% in February 2026, and 13.2% in August 2025 — KBRA's universe differs from Trepp's broader dataset and consistently reads higher

S&P Global Ratings headline noted 'The Office Rate Surpasses 10.5%' for January 2026 overall CMBS — paywalled detail, directionally consistent but numerically below both Trepp and KBRA office readings

regional_bank_stress.fact: Forbes Advisor (sourcing FDIC data, updated 2026) reports 4 US bank failures year-to-date in 2026: Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust (Jan 30, $261M assets, CRE-linked per Bisnow Feb 2 2026), Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia (May 1, preceded by FDIC enforcement action April 2026), Kentland Federal Savings and Loan (Jul 10), and a fourth unnamed institution. At least 3 of these 4 fall within the trailing 6-month window (Feb 17 - Aug 17 2026). FDIC/Bisnow confirm CRE real-estate loan exposure as a contributing factor for Metropolitan Capital; the FDIC issued a pre-closure enforcement action against Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia in April 2026.
regional_bank_stress.rationale: The rubric threshold for CLUSTER is >=3 failures in 6 months; at least 3 of the 4 2026 failures fall in the trailing 6-month window, each with assets well below $10bn, satisfying the count criterion mechanically. Additionally, the April 2026 FDIC enforcement action preceding Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia's May closure independently satisfies the ISOLATED threshold, but the >=3 count elevates the reading to CLUSTER=2. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (2 vs 0); held for review]

dissent.view: Bankrate (Feb 18 2026 update) reported only 1 failure in 2026 at that time (Metropolitan Capital), and did not confirm CRE as the primary regulatory cited cause; FDIC has not released a formal post-seizure analysis citing CRE concentration for any 2026 failure as of this date, leaving causal attribution partially inferential.

govt_stability.fact: PM Sébastien Lecornu's minority government survived two no-confidence motions on 2 February 2026 — the final pair tied to the 2026 budget passage — with the LFI-led motion drawing 260 votes vs. the 289 needed, and the RN motion drawing only 135 votes; the 2026 budget was formally adopted the same day. Lecornu governs without a parliamentary majority, relying on Socialist and Les Républicains abstentions. Source: Al Jazeera, 2026-02-02 (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/2/france-adopts-2026-budget-after-two-no-confidence-votes-fail); Reuters via Yahoo, 2026-01-27 (https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/french-government-survives-no-confidence-190649618.html).
govt_stability.rationale: Lecornu holds no working majority and repeatedly invoked Article 49.3-equivalent constitutional bypass mechanisms, survived multiple no-confidence votes across Oct 2025–Feb 2026, and governs through targeted concessions — a paradigmatic FRAGILE (1) situation. No evidence of a government collapse, PM resignation, or snap election call has emerged since the budget passage on 2 February 2026.

dissent.view: A Yahoo/AP report (~March 2026) references Bayrou announcing a confidence vote for 8 September — but corroborating sources confirm Bayrou fell on 8 September 2025 (pre-Lecornu), making this a timeline artefact rather than a competing current reading.

rating_action.fact: Fitch Ratings downgraded France's sovereign credit rating from 'AA-' to 'A+' with a stable outlook on ~12 September 2025, citing a high and rising debt ratio and political fragmentation hindering fiscal consolidation (source: CNBC, FXStreet, ING Think, September 15 2025). Moody's also held Aa3 with negative outlook (Oct 2025) and S&P held AA- with negative outlook (Mar 2025 action, confirmed Nov 2025).
rating_action.rationale: Fitch executed an actual one-notch rating cut (AA- to A+) in September 2025, squarely within the trailing 12 months from today (2026-08-17), which maps directly to rubric band 2 (DOWNGRADE). Moody's negative outlook and S&P negative outlook would independently qualify for band 1, but the Fitch downgrade is the most severe observed action.

dissent.view: Moody's maintained Aa3 (no downgrade in trailing 12m, only negative outlook as of Oct 2025) and S&P maintained AA- (no downgrade in trailing 12m, negative outlook from Mar 2025) — these alone would score band 1, not 2

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch Ratings subprime auto ABS 60-day-plus delinquency rate in June 2026 was 5.67%, down 64 basis points year-over-year, per Wolf Street (August 13, 2026) citing Fitch Ratings directly.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The Fitch ABS index is the primary, authoritative source for securitized subprime auto 60+ DPD; June 2026 at 5.67% is the latest published monthly figure, well above historical norms but meaningfully off the January 2026 record peak of 6.90%, reflecting seasonal improvement while remaining structurally elevated.

dissent.view: January 2026 peak reading of 6.90% (record high, 32-year) per Fitch Ratings — still cited in some July 2026 commentary as the headline figure without updating to June
Philadelphia Fed Q3 2025 consumer-level 60+ DPD (all auto, not subprime-only) peaked at 1.68% — different universe and methodology than Fitch ABS index

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm 30+ DPD on monthly installment loans ex-Peloton was 2.8% as of March 31, 2026, up 29 bps YoY from 2.5% at March 31, 2025 (Affirm FQ3'26 SEC 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001820953/000162828026032105/affirmfq326shareholderle.htm, filed May 7, 2026). CFPB/Richmond Fed data show sector charge-off rate at ~1.83% in 2023, rising modestly since but remaining well below 3%.
bnpl_delinq.rationale: 30+ DPD is up 29 bps YoY (rising, not flat/down), placing it above the Level 0 threshold; however the +29 bps increase is far below the +100 bps trigger for Level 2, and charge-offs per CFPB data remain ~1.8-2%, contained well under the 3% cap for Level 1.

dissent.view: Richmond Fed (Feb 2026) notes 'indicative evidence from consumer surveys that late payment and delinquency behavior among BNPL users has increased since 2023' but cites no hard YoY bps figure rivaling Affirm's audited filing; Klarna reports delinquency rates 'continuing to decline' per its own 2025 press release, diverging from the Affirm upward trend.

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (published July 1, 2026): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.' Source: https://data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20july%201
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric asks for the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the IMF's own COFER Data Brief dated July 1, 2026 reports exactly 57.13% for 2026Q1, which is the most recent published quarter and maps directly to the indicator.

dissent.view: coferdata.com displays USD share at 56.77% — likely using prior-quarter or interpolated data rather than the official IMF July 1, 2026 release

weaponization_event.fact: As of April 2026 (IAI/Brookings), the EU chose joint debt issuance over outright confiscation of ~€210bn in frozen Russian CBR assets; no new sovereign reserve seizure executed in 2026. Separately, BRICS Pay pilot launch is targeted for the end-2026 India summit, but bricspayment.ru (the official tracker) notes the system 'remains in the planning and early-pilot stage' with full operational status pegged to 2030 by Russian Deputy FM Ryabkov.
weaponization_event.rationale: No new sovereign reserve freeze or confiscation has been executed in 2026; the Russian assets remain frozen under the 2022 regime and the EU explicitly opted against outright seizure in Dec 2025. BRICS Pay and the BRICS Unit gold-settlement pilot represent active non-dollar settlement launches/rhetoric but fall short of a major economy operationally moving reserve settlement off USD, placing the indicator squarely at band 1 (TALK/early-pilot).

dissent.view: Some secondary sources (watcher.guru, informedclearly.com) characterize BRICS Pay as already 'operational' in 2026 with intra-bloc local currency trade at 67%, which could imply a band-2 shift; however these sources lack primary central-bank confirmation and contradict the official BRICS Pay tracker and EBC Financial Group's April 2026 assessment that no operationally dominant alternative settlement system is live.

insurer_exits.fact: NAIC 'Examining Homeowner Property Insurance Market Dynamics' report (July 31, 2026) covering 715 carriers and 2018-2024 MCAS data: company-initiated non-renewal rates rose 96%-216% across all four US regions; approximately 13 states (CA, FL, TX, LA, CO, GA, OK, and others) are documented with active non-renewal waves or significant carrier book reductions, per NAIC + Climate Cosmos (June 2026). NAIC characterises the market as 'operationally robust but under pressure.' Florida Citizens depopulated from 1.42M to ~385K-395K policies by Jan 2026, indicating partial stabilisation. No confirmed full exit of a top-10 insurer from a major state in 2026.
insurer_exits.rationale: ~13 states with active non-renewal/market-retreat conditions sits in the 5-15 band triggering rubric level 1 (RISING); the absence of a confirmed top-10 full-state exit and evidence of FL stabilisation prevents escalation to level 2 (ACCELERATING).

dissent.view: Climate Cosmos (June 18, 2026) enumerates exactly 13 named states with insurer drop waves, which is near the upper bound of the RISING band and could tip to ACCELERATING if additional states are confirmed in the NAIC ZIP-level data call launched March 2026.
insurance.com survey (May 2026) reports only 7% of homeowners experienced non-renewal/cancellation, characterising numbers as 'very low,' implying the systemic severity may be overstated.

cat_losses.fact: Swiss Re Institute estimates global insured natural catastrophe losses at USD 42 billion for H1 2026, 16% below the 10-year first-half average of USD 50 billion — the lowest H1 total since 2020. Munich Re reports USD 44 billion (also below the 10-year average of ~USD 50 billion). Gallagher Re reports at least USD 46 billion, 28% below the 10-year average. No single event exceeded USD 5 billion in insured losses in H1 2026. Sources: Swiss Re Institute (swissre.com, ~2026-08-11); Munich Re (munichre.com, 2026-07-30); Gallagher Re via Risk & Insurance (~2026-07-15).
cat_losses.rationale: H1 2026 insured cat losses of USD 42–47bn are uniformly below the 10-year first-half average (~USD 50bn), placing YTD at roughly 84–94% of average — well under the 150% threshold for SEVERE and also below the average itself. No single event exceeded USD 10bn, ruling out the ELEVATED trigger on the single-event criterion. Rubric maps cleanly to 0 = NORMAL.

dissent.view: Aon estimates H1 2026 insured losses at 'at least $47bn', slightly above Swiss Re's $42bn and Munich Re's $44bn, but still characterises losses as below the 10-year average

ss_reform_news.fact: 2026 SSA Trustees Report (ssa.gov/oact/TR/2026/, released 2026-06-09): OASI trust fund projected depleted Q4 2032 (one quarter earlier than 2025 report); combined OASDI depletion 2034; 75-year actuarial deficit widened to 4.42% of taxable payroll. No benefit cuts enacted or automatically triggered; reform bills (H.R. 9187 Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act; Senate PROMISE Act) introduced but not voted on.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report materially worsened the depletion outlook and reform is actively debated in Congress, satisfying band 1 (DEBATE). No automatic trigger has fired and no legislation enacting cuts has been enacted, so band 2 (CUTS) is not met.

dissent.view: CBO (Feb 2026) estimates a steeper 28% automatic cut vs. SSA trustees estimate of 22% upon OASI depletion, reflecting different economic assumptions; depletion date agreed at 2032.

pension_leverage_event.fact: ESMA June 2026 stress-test report (ESMA50-1949966494-4208, published 23 Jun 2026) finds LDI fund resilience has improved since the 2022 crisis: the liquidity shortfall under stress declined from EUR 9bn to EUR 3bn by end-2024, driven by reduced leverage and lower NAV (EUR 113bn vs EUR 130bn at crisis). No forced gilt selling or central-bank intervention has been reported in 2026; the January 2025 gilt sell-off produced cash calls but was described by industry advisers and BlackRock as 'orderly' with no forced asset sales.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: ESMA's most recent formal assessment (Jun 2026) confirms improved liquidity buffers and no active margin crisis; absent any regulator flag of current LDI liquidity risk or a documented forced-selling episode in 2026, the evidence maps squarely to rubric band 0 (buffers adequate, no margin stress).

dissent.view: ESMA's end-2024 data notes 'a subset of funds might still face challenges' under extreme shocks, implying residual tail risk that has not been fully eliminated

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): funded ratio of the 100 largest U.S. public pension plans was 88.7% as of June 30, 2026 (assets $6.116T vs. TPL $6.894T). Source: Milliman, https://www.milliman.com/en/insight/public-pension-funding-index-july-2026, published July 30, 2026.
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the most comprehensive monthly mark-to-market measure of the 100 largest U.S. public DB plans; 88.7% maps directly to the rubric as the representative funded ratio. The Equable Institute independently reports 85.0% for a broader 253-plan universe as of the same date, confirming the general band. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-06-30 data but the prior applied value was FY2026 (as of 2026-07-23) data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' projects the national average funded ratio at 85.0% for FY2026 (as of June 30, 2026) across 253 statewide and municipal plans — lower than Milliman because the universe includes smaller, more underfunded plans.

interconnection_months.fact: The median U.S. project that reached commercial operation in 2025 spent 61 months in the interconnection queue (IR to COD), per LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (data through end of 2025, published June 2026). Primary source: https://emp.lbl.gov/queues and https://emp.lbl.gov/publications/queued-2026-edition-characteristics
interconnection_months.rationale: LBNL's 2026 Edition is the most current authoritative report; the 61-month median IR-to-COD for projects built in 2025 is the load-bearing figure and maps directly to the rubric's request for latest median wait in months. A secondary figure of 45 months (IR to signed interconnection agreement, not COD) exists but measures a different milestone and is not used as the primary value.

dissent.view: 45 months median from interconnection request to signed interconnection agreement (not IR to COD) for 2025, per LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition as cited by Axis Intelligence — a different milestone than IR-to-COD

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed an executive order on July 14, 2026 imposing the nation's first statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers (>=50 MW), pausing environmental permits for up to one year. Separately, the NY legislature passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642/A11560) on June 4, 2026 (Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39), which has not yet been signed into statute. Beyond NY: Maine's legislature passed a moratorium in April 2026 (vetoed by Gov. Mills); Texas Gov. Abbott issued a directive on Aug. 3, 2026 pausing new data center grid connections pending an ERCOT/PUCT audit; >100 local moratoria adopted nationwide; at least 11-12 states introduced moratorium bills; and DLA Piper (July 1, 2026) reports 'more than 100 local moratoria have been adopted nationwide' with 'at least 12 states [having] considered moratorium legislation.' Sources: Axios/NY Gov. press release July 14 2026; DLA Piper July 1 2026; Houston Public Media Aug. 3 2026.
dc_moratoria.rationale: A confirmed statewide moratorium is now in force in New York via executive order (signed July 14, 2026), plus Texas has enacted a grid-connection pause directive (Aug. 3, 2026), and >100 local jurisdictions have enacted pauses — this decisively meets rubric level 2 ('a statewide moratorium enacted, OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses/cancellations').

dissent.view: The NY legislative bill (Responsible Data Center Development Act) has not been signed into statute as of mid-August 2026; Hochul chose executive order over the bill, which some analysts say is narrower in scope (50 MW threshold vs. bill's 20 MW). Maine's statewide moratorium was vetoed. Ohio's ballot initiative failed.

ai_power_pressure.fact: DOE issued three separate Section 202(c) emergency orders to PJM Interconnection in 2026 (Jan 26, May 18, and a third by July 4) authorizing curtailment of data-center backup-generator loads as a last resort before rolling blackouts; New York Gov. Hochul imposed a statewide data-center moratorium on July 14, 2026; Seattle enacted an emergency moratorium June 9, 2026; and Texas Gov. Abbott called for a full ERCOT data-center queue audit on Aug 3, 2026 — halting Batch Zero reviews — against a 474 GW queue. Sources: DOE.gov (Jan 26 2026), UtilityDive/PJM (May 18 2026), TechTimes (Jul 4 2026), Sheppard/NY Executive Order (Jul 14 2026), UtilityDive/Texas (Aug 5 2026).
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Multiple confirmed physical and regulatory events satisfy the rubric's Level 2 threshold: DOE-authorized curtailment of data-center load under declared grid emergencies in PJM (three times in 2026), plus power-scarcity-driven state moratoria in New York and Seattle and a de facto Texas queue freeze — all go well beyond warnings or forecasts. The IEA's 'Key Questions on Energy and AI' (2026) corroborates, noting slow grid connections are already forcing developers onto on-site gas generation.

dissent.view: FERC June 18 2026 order directing all six RTOs to fast-track large-load interconnection could shorten queues and ease conditions in 2H 2026, potentially moving the indicator back toward Level 1 if reforms take hold quickly

mine_disruptions.fact: As of mid-2026, at least three top-20 copper mines carry confirmed, active production cuts: (1) Grasberg (world\'s #2 copper mine) — Freeport delayed full restart to early 2028, targeting only ~65% capacity in H2 2026 vs. pre-incident ~1.7 billion lb/yr; copper output guided at ~700 million lb in 2026, down ~59% from plan (mining.com, May 8 2026). (2) Kamoa-Kakula (DRC, top-5 mine) — seismic/flood damage in 2025 cut 2026 guidance to 290,000–330,000 t vs. original 420,000–600,000 t target; Q2 2026 actual output was 64,328 t (Ivanhoe Q2 release, July 8 2026). (3) Codelco El Teniente (world\'s largest underground copper mine) — fatal tunnel collapse in 2025 led general manager to state production will be depressed for the next five years (CNBC, March 10 2026). Additional disruptions: Capstone Mantoverde strike (halted Jan 2026); CMOC TFM strike (June 2026); Chilean output down 9% YoY in March 2026 (Cochilco). Multiple institutions forecast a 2026 market deficit: ICSG revised from a 209,000 t surplus to a 150,000 t deficit; J.P. Morgan 330,000 t deficit; Morgan Stanley 600,000 t; ING 600,000 t (cruxinvestor.com, May 26 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Three or more named top-20 mines (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, El Teniente) have confirmed, physically measured production cuts active in 2026, and multiple major financial institutions have revised global copper balances to a deficit — both prongs of the rubric\'s CLUSTER threshold (value=2) are satisfied.

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 Copper Market Forecast projects a refined copper market surplus of 96,000 metric tons for full-year 2026, reversing its prior October 2025 forecast of a 150,000t deficit; preliminary ICSG Q1 2026 data (May 2026 bulletin) showed an actual oversupply of ~396,000mt. Source: ICSG April 2026 forecast via admis.com (2026-04-24), recyclingtoday.com (2026-04-28), metalnomist.com (2026-07); ICSG May 2026 monthly bulletin via news.metal.com (2026-05-22).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: The ICSG April 2026 full-year forecast of +96,000t surplus falls just within the rubric's ±100kt balanced band (96kt < 100kt threshold), mapping to score 1 (BALANCED); however, Q1 2026 preliminary actuals of ~396,000t oversupply skew the physical balance firmly toward surplus, creating ambiguity at the boundary.

dissent.view: ICSG October 2025 forecast projected a 150,000t refined copper DEFICIT for 2026, driven by concentrate supply constraints and slower refined production growth - this was the prevailing view before the April 2026 revision.
Q1 2026 ICSG preliminary data showed actual oversupply of ~396,000mt, far exceeding the full-year +96kt forecast and strongly suggesting a full-year SURPLUS outcome well outside the balanced band.
ICSG April 2025 (pre-revision) had forecast a 209kt surplus for 2026; ING reported this as the baseline before October 2025 revision to deficit.

drought_chip_farm.fact: US Drought Monitor data (via NDMC/plantmaps, Aug 8 2026): Arizona shows 47.3% of state in D2 Severe Drought and 1.5% in D3 Extreme Drought; no confirmed fab or farm production curtailment order found. Taiwan: no current drought emergency or fab water-rationing identified.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: D2 (Severe) dominates Arizona - a key US Southwest chip-fab and farming region - satisfying the rubric threshold for rating 1 (EMERGING). D3 exists but covers only ~1.5% of the state and no confirmed production curtailment has been identified, so rating 2 is not justified.

dissent.view: June 30 2026 USDM Arizona PDF showed ~61% in D2 and ~1.47% in D3, a slightly worse picture than Aug 8 reading, consistent with some monsoon improvement since then
Aug 2026 monsoon outlook (drought.gov, Aug 13 2026) notes drought conditions improving in parts of Southwest due to active monsoon, suggesting the Aug 8 D2 reading may soften further

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,039.82 ft, storage 6,965,290 acre-feet = 26.7% of 26,120,000 AF capacity, per Bureau of Reclamation daily gauge data via ReservoirBench.com (Aug 12 2026); this broke the all-time record low set Aug 6 2026 at 1,040.50 ft; Hoover Dam minimum power pool is 1,050 ft, meaning the lake is ~10 ft below that operational threshold.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.7% of capacity the reservoir is unambiguously below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold; at ~1,039-1,040 ft it is already ~10-11 ft below Hoover Dam's minimum power pool of 1,050 ft, constituting a confirmed physical operational impact, not merely a forecast.

dissent.view: Colorado River Monitor reports 28.5% capacity as of 2026-08-15, slightly higher than the 26.7% reading from ReservoirBench — difference likely reflects differing capacity basis or lag in data refresh, but both readings are well below the 30% critical threshold

water_dispute.fact: India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty 'in abeyance' after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, physically cut flows via Baglihar Dam on the Chenab (May 2025), stopped hydrological data sharing, and Pakistan reported abrupt flow drops at Marala (Chenab: 21,887 to 5,689 cusecs) in May 2026. Pakistan's Defence Minister stated 'the moment we feel our national security is under threat...we will go to war' (June 2026 CNBC). India's Home Minister vowed the treaty 'will never be restored' (June 2025, reiterated 2026). Sources: Chatham House April 2026; CNBC June 22 2026; Dawn June 2026; Britannica July 2026.
water_dispute.rationale: A deliberate flow cut-off was physically carried out (Baglihar Dam, May 2025 confirmed), the treaty is formally suspended/in abeyance with India rejecting arbitration awards, and Pakistan's Defence Minister issued an explicit war threat directly tied to water/dam control in June 2026 — all three crisis-level triggers in the rubric are met. The GERD/Nile dispute remains at level 1 (contested legal framework, official threats, no kinetic action or flow cut-off), but the Indus situation is the binding constraint at level 2.

dissent.view: GERD/Nile dispute assessed as TENSE (level 1) not CRISIS: Egypt raised GERD at UNSC and signed military port agreements with Eritrea/Djibouti (strategic posturing), but no armed clash or deliberate Nile flow cut-off has occurred; analysts (pppescp.com, March 2026) assess armed conflict likelihood as 'relatively low'.
Chatham House (April 2026) frames IWT suspension as 'temporary' and calls for re-engagement, suggesting some analysts view the situation as still short of full crisis.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 131.1 points in July 2026, up 0.6% MoM from June's 130.3 and up 1.0% YoY. Released 7 August 2026. Source: fao.org/newsroom/detail/fao-food-price-index-edges-up-amid-weather--energy-and-geopolitical-concerns/en
fao_food_trend.rationale: The index is rising both MoM (+0.6%) and YoY (+1.0%), and sits at a 3-year high (131.1), firmly placing it in the ELEVATED band; the MoM gain of 0.6% is well below the 3% threshold required for band 1's upper boundary and far below the 5% MoM or 10% 3-month thresholds needed for SPIKING (band 2). The 3-month cumulative move (Mar 128.5 → Jul 131.1) is roughly +2%, also below the 10% SPIKING trigger.

china_export_curbs.fact: NDRC suspended phosphate fertilizer (DAP, MAP, NPK) exports through August 2026 per a December 11, 2025 NDRC-directed industry meeting; in mid-March 2026 Beijing extended curbs to nitrogen-potassium blends and additional phosphate varieties; as of July 29, 2026 Fertilizer Daily reports curbs extended 'at least through August 2026'. Urea: export inspections suspended March-April 2026; NDRC issued ~1.5-1.6 mt quota for June-August on May 26, 2026 with $660/mt FOB price floor (Profercy/Keyuan Fertilizer, May 26-29 2026). Between 50-80% of China's fertilizer export volumes remain restricted (Reuters/Fertilizer Daily, July 29 2026).
china_export_curbs.rationale: Active phosphate suspension (NDRC Dec 2025, extended to Aug 2026) and urea under tight quota-with-price-floor regime confirm restrictions are IN PLACE. The most recent tightening event — mid-March 2026 expansion to NK blends — falls ~5 months ago, just outside the 3-month window for rating 2; the July 29 phosphate extension is a continuation of the existing suspension, not a new product category, so rubric score is 1 not 2.

dissent.view: Fertilizer Daily (Jul 29 2026) headline frames the phosphate curb 'extension through August 2026' as a new event within the 3-month window, which could support a score of 2 if interpreted as a broadened/renewed restriction rather than a continuation

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-08-09 vs. a pre-crisis baseline of 73/day; on the weekend of Aug 16-17 only 0-5 ships passed vs. 31 the prior weekend (CNBC, 2026-08-17; straits.live, 2026-08-17). The 60-day US-Iran ceasefire expired Aug 17 with no deal and talks stalled. Brent crude at $88.31/bbl on Aug 17, ~32.6% above year-ago levels (TradingEconomics, 2026-08-17). Persian Gulf supplies ~44% of seaborne sulfur, ~43% of urea, and >25% of global ammonia exports (NDSU Agricultural Trade Monitor, March 2026); these flows are effectively halted.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: The strait meets the rubric's CLOSED (2) threshold: transit volumes are at or near zero with no active truce or escorted convoy operation, and Brent crude is materially elevated (~33% YoY), satisfying the required corroborating price signal. No convoys moving and no signed ceasefire cap this at 1; all three CUT conditions are met.

dissent.view: Iran and Oman reported to be 'working on a temporary shipping route' (Middle East Eye, unverified/single-source, Aug 16) — if a deal materialises intraday this could revert to 1

taiwan_tension.fact: Beijing launched a two-day live-fire drill in the Taiwan Strait on July 24-25, 2026, in waters near Dongshan Island within 12km of the mainland coast, triggered by President Lai Ching-te's speech that Taiwan was 'not subordinate to the PRC'; no named large-scale encirclement exercise, no blockade, no kinetic clash reported as of Aug 14, 2026 (South China Morning Post, July 23, 2026; CFR Global Conflict Tracker, Aug 2026; Heritage/Daily Signal, July 31, 2026).
taiwan_tension.rationale: The July 2026 live-fire drill is assertive and politically motivated but geographically confined to nearshore Fujian waters rather than encircling Taiwan; no blockade or kinetic clash was recorded, placing it squarely at Rubric 1 (ELEVATED). Analysts noted a relative lull in major named PLA exercises post-drill, with the median line still routinely crossed but no escalation to Crisis-level activity.

dissent.view: Heritage Foundation/Daily Signal (July 31, 2026) characterises the post-July period as a 'lull' expected to be temporary, implying current activity may be closer to elevated-routine rather than a distinct escalation event.

export_controls.fact: US side: House Foreign Affairs Committee passed 20 export control measures incl. MATCH Act (April 24, 2026, SCMP) targeting DUV lithography to China; Commerce Sec. Lutnick held private meetings pressing ASML on EUV compliance (June 2026, Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance); ASML China revenue share fell 36%->19% Q4-2025 to Q1-2026 confirming volume impact. China side: April 2026 'Regulations on Countering Improper Extraterritorial Jurisdiction' empower Beijing to deem ASML compliance with US FDP Rule illegal (JustSecurity/justsecurity.org, July 2026); Jan 2026 rare-earth export control catalogue expansion; Aug 5 2026 drone export control countermeasures (geopolitechs.org).
export_controls.rationale: Both sides have enacted measures in the trailing 3 months: the US advanced legislative tightening (MATCH Act committee passage) and intensified ASML compliance pressure, while China enacted legal counter-controls (extraterritorial jurisdiction regulations) designed to prohibit ASML and similar firms from complying with US FDP rules, constituting legal retaliation per the rubric. Rating is capped at 2 rather than higher because China's semiconductor-specific counter-controls remain regulatory/legal rather than an outright equipment ban, and no secondary market price dislocation attributable solely to Chinese countermeasures has been confirmed.

dissent.view: East Asia Forum (March 2026) argues the Trump White House deliberately cooled chip export control escalation in H1 2026, approving H200 exports and suspending new restrictions to prioritise trade talks — suggesting the net posture is tightening-only (Level 1), not full retaliation.
Wilson Sonsini (Jan 2026) notes BIS actually eased some advanced chip controls to China on Jan 14, 2026 (H200/MI325X case-by-case review), complicating a pure 'tightening' narrative on the US side.

fab_concentration.fact: As of August 2026, TSMC's entire <=3nm capacity (2nm: ~50k-60k wpm; 3nm: ~150k wpm) is in Taiwan. Arizona Fab 21 Phase 1 produces N4 (4nm), Phase 2 construction completed April 2026 with 3nm equipment installation only beginning Q3 2026 and volume production targeted H2 2027. Japan JASM runs 12/16nm. Zero overseas <=3nm operational capacity. Source: TSMC.com Arizona page (July 2026 update); TrendForce Aug 3 2026; Quantumrun TSMC Statistics June 22 2026.
fab_concentration.rationale: All <=3nm/2nm output is exclusively in Taiwan fabs, with overseas leading-edge production (Arizona 3nm) not commencing until H2 2027 at earliest; this places the outside-Taiwan share at effectively 0%, well below the 10% threshold, and no operational overseas leading-edge fab exists — the rubric's EXTREME condition (score=2) is met unambiguously. The 30% US share projection applies only to a post-2030 multi-fab buildout scenario.

dissent.view: TrendForce (Dec 2023) projected Taiwan's advanced-process share declining to ~60% and US rising to 17% by 2027, implying a faster diversification trajectory than current status reflects — but these were forward projections, not realized capacity figures.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: Kpler data cited by IranWire/Reuters (2026-08-17): only 5 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday Aug 15 and zero on Sunday Aug 16, against a pre-crisis baseline of ~73/day (PortWatch). Brent crude rose to $89.40/bbl on Aug 17 driven by 'a drastic reduction in tanker transit.' The IRGC has formally closed the strait to 'unfriendly nations' since 2 March 2026; a June MOU collapsed in early July; US-Iran talks remain deadlocked as of Aug 17. (Sources: IranWire citing Reuters, 2026-08-17; straits.live, 2026-08-17; PortWatch/IMF; Lloyd's List Intelligence, 2026-08-05.)
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Transit volumes are 0–7% of the pre-crisis baseline (0–5 ships vs ~73/day), well below the rubric's 25% threshold, with no functioning convoy workaround; Brent at ~$89/bbl confirms a sustained supply-risk premium consistent with a near-closure, satisfying the rubric's market-signal corroboration requirement for a rating of 2.

dissent.view: US CENTCOM claims ~9 million b/d still passing through the waterway (implying meaningful residual flow), and some dark-AIS tankers are moving; Trading Economics (2026-08-14) notes crude 'is still moving out of the Persian Gulf' via transponder-off vessels — suggesting 'contested' rather than fully closed.

Lloyd's List Intelligence (2026-08-05) recorded 84 transits in the week of 27 Jul–2 Aug, a partial recovery from 45 the prior week, indicating the strait is severely disrupted but not at zero — closer to contested.

cable_incidents.fact: Geneva Solutions (May 18 2026) reported: 'A second incident in September 2025 damaged four more cables, one of which is still out of service' -- referring to the Sep 6 2025 Red Sea cuts (SEA-ME-WE-4, IMEWE, FALCON, EIG); repair status unresolved as of mid-May 2026 per that source. No subsequent confirmed repair announcement found as of 2026-08-17.
cable_incidents.rationale: At least one major cable (from the Sep 6 2025 Red Sea multi-cable event) remained severed and unrepaired as of May 2026, satisfying rubric level 2 (>=1 major cable currently severed and unrepaired causing connectivity loss). Hormuz cables face credible Iranian threats but no confirmed cut, and Baltic incidents are ongoing but largely characterised as anchor-drag investigations rather than confirmed major severed trunks. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-05-18 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08-10 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: Hormuz cables intact as of May 2026 -- CNN and Jerusalem Post report only IRGC-linked threats, not an actual cut; rubric-2 does not apply to Hormuz corridor

Baltic January 2026 Lithuania-Latvia cable (Arelion) damage treated as under investigation / anchor-drag incident, not confirmed hostile severance of major international trunk -- closer to rubric level 1

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SEC Commissioner Uyeda August 2026 update (sec.gov, ~Aug 7 2026) confirms Dec 31 2026 cash and Jun 30 2027 repo deadlines hold, but multiple exemptive relief requests remain pending (SIFMA inter-affiliate, IIB non-U.S. transactions, 15c3-3 omnibus margin relief with comments due Aug 31 2026); TBAC May 2026 report identifies 'largest challenge continues to be the amount of legal work and documentation associated with bilateral agreements between participants'; DTCC/FICC readiness survey (~July 2026) shows 79% of netting members have account structures in place and 'most respondents already prepared or completing final readiness activities', but $300-400bn in daily cash activity still to migrate (source: sec.gov Uyeda Aug 2026 statement; home.treasury.gov TBACCharge1Q22026.pdf May 2026; finadium.com DTCC survey ~Jul 2026).
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: Multiple exemptive relief requests are actively pending and unresolved (SIFMA, IIB, 15c3-3) and a legal/documentation backlog for bilateral agreements is the cited top implementation challenge — both conditions map directly to rubric Score 1 (FRICTION). No deadline extension has been granted and readiness surveys show >80% confidence among netting members, ruling out Score 2. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-08-17 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: DTCC/FICC president Brian Steele states 'the industry is well positioned for the Treasury cash clearing deadline on December 31, 2026' with 79% account structures in place and $12T+ daily clearing volume — suggesting Score 0 (SMOOTH) is plausible for cash.

TBAC May 2026 warns 'challenges associated with some remaining issues could result in a clearing market not available to all participants in all regions by the SEC deadline' and CME go-live slipped Q2 to Q3 2026 — suggesting Score 2 (PROBLEMS) risk is non-trivial for repo.
